headline: High-risk data leakage and capability conflict: OpenHands can read/write runtime files and use MCP, while Chatwoot handles customer data and broad egress.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: OpenHands can use MCP and read/write runtime files, so if Chatwoot content is bridged into its workspace or an MCP channel, prompt-like instructions could be injected. Chatwoot itself exposes customer-facing messages and integrations, but no direct shared channel is documented, so this is a plausible but not proven interaction.
conditions: IF Chatwoot outputs are copied into an OpenHands workspace or MCP server
IF OpenHands parses Chatwoot content as instructions rather than data
mitigations: Disable any automatic ingestion of Chatwoot exports into OpenHands
Require a human review step before OpenHands acts on Chatwoot text
Use a dedicated, read-only staging folder for transferred content
Restrict MCP servers to trusted, provenance-tagged sources
requires-engineering: add content provenance labels between the systems

B_data_leakage.rationale: Chatwoot touches customer data, contact profiles, interaction history, orders, and messages, while OpenHands can read files, run browsers, and use broad network egress. If customer records are mounted into OpenHands, its default toolset can exfiltrate them to external services or model providers. The pair therefore creates a direct leakage path.
conditions: IF customer data from Chatwoot is mounted into the OpenHands runtime
IF OpenHands is allowed to send runtime contents to external model providers or websites
mitigations: Do not mount customer datasets into OpenHands by default
Use redacted or synthetic samples for any OpenHands task
Block outbound network access except to approved endpoints
Separate Chatwoot production data from OpenHands runtimes
requires-engineering: enforce per-file data classification and egress policy

C_capability_conflict.rationale: OpenHands has write_filesystem and modify_git_state, and its concurrency model says shared state is via mounted volume only. Chatwoot is not shown with write access, so the conflict is mainly when both are pointed at the same mounted workspace or repo. That overlap can corrupt files or git state, but the profiles do not show unrestricted shared writes by both agents.
conditions: IF Chatwoot exports are written into the same mounted directory OpenHands edits
IF OpenHands and Chatwoot both mutate the same git repository or workspace
mitigations: Use separate directories for Chatwoot exports and OpenHands workspaces
Make shared mounts read-only unless a task explicitly needs writes
Avoid letting OpenHands operate on live production repos
Serialize edits with a simple lock file or manual handoff
requires-engineering: add workspace-level locking and conflict detection

D_cascading_error.rationale: Chatwoot can produce customer-support content and reports, and OpenHands can act on files and browser state. If Chatwoot output is fed into OpenHands as authoritative input, OpenHands may execute or transform incorrect support content without verification. The pair lacks a documented verification boundary, so the cascade is plausible in default workflows.
conditions: IF Chatwoot-generated text is passed to OpenHands as trusted task input
IF OpenHands is allowed to act without a separate verification step
mitigations: Insert a human approval step before OpenHands acts on Chatwoot output
Require OpenHands to cite source files before taking action
Use a validation checklist for any support-response generation
Limit OpenHands to drafting only, not sending or committing
requires-engineering: add automated verification against source records

E_compliance.rationale: Chatwoot handles customer data and interaction history, while OpenHands handles files in its runtime and may send them to a configured model provider. If regulated customer data is moved from Chatwoot into OpenHands, residency and retention obligations can diverge. The profiles do not prove a violation, but they do show a compliance mismatch risk.
conditions: IF regulated customer data is transferred from Chatwoot into OpenHands
IF OpenHands runtime retention or provider residency differs from Chatwoot policy
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of OpenHands runtimes
Use anonymized exports for debugging and coding tasks
Document retention and deletion rules for both systems
Restrict OpenHands to non-production datasets
requires-engineering: align residency and retention controls across both tools
